title: Failchain sleuth: repro notes and command log
content:
Summary:
This is my working scratchpad for a recurring failure we see on a small subset of inference nodes: intermittent GPU OOMs in relatively small batches, but only for certain container images. Symptoms sometimes include a CUDA driver/library mismatch (symbol lookup errors) immediately after container startup, or a sudden CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY on first allocation. Hypothesis: multiple versions of libcuda / CUDA runtime artifacts are being mixed between host, container base image, and nvidia-container-toolkit mountpoints. Also possible: stale LD_PRELOAD or autopatched symlinks from packaging/CI.

Environment baseline:
- Host driver: NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.05 (driver 535.86.05)
- Host kernel: 6.5.0-21-generic
- Common container base: nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-runtime-ubuntu22.04 (but failing runs sometimes use 12.1 images)
- nvidia-container-toolkit: 1.13.0 (host)
- runtime: containerd + nvidia-container-runtime-hook
- ML stack: PyTorch 2.2.0 (built with CUDA 12.1) and bitsandbytes 0.39.0 (libbitsandbytes.so loaded at runtime)

Repro minimal (observed):
1) Start the container with default runtime and run this snippet:

python - <<'PY'
import torch
print(torch.version.cuda)
print(torch.cuda.is_available())
# allocate a moderate tensor to trigger driver allocation path
a = torch.randn((1024, 1024, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)
print(a.numel())
PY

- On healthy hosts this completes and prints reasonably. On affected hosts it either fails with allocation OOM or the process aborts with an unresolved symbol error when importing torch.

Observed error snippets (copied from failing runs):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 64.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 30.00 GiB already allocated; 2.56 GiB free; 29.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: undefined symbol: cuMemAlloc_v2"
- "CUDA ERROR: unknown error (303)"
- dmesg kernel note: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f.0): 31, Xid (n)"
- "cuInit(): CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN" during torch.cuda.init()

Commands I ran and outputs (high level):
1) nvidia-smi -a
   - Driver: 535.86.05, GPUs healthy, processes show container pids attached.
2) nvcc --version inside container images
   - In failing image: reports CUDA 12.1; base image reports 12.2 in different builds.
3) ldd on python extension that binds to cuda (libtorch_cuda.so)
   - ldd shows libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host-mounted)
   - Also found /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1 inside container image; mismatch between libcudart (runtime) and libcuda (driver) can be ok but warnings surfaced when libcuda is unexpected version.
4) ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* (host)
   - symlink chain: libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1 -> ../../libnvidia-ml.so.1 (packaging specifics differ across nodes)
5) strace -e open,stat,read -f python -c 'import torch'
   - Observed early open of /etc/ld.so.preload on some hosts that contained an entry managed by a profiling agent; on failing hosts this preload points to an older libshim that wraps libcuda.
6) grep -R "libcuda" /var/log/* 
   - Found post-install scripts that created /usr/local/lib/libcuda.so symlink in older images; container runtime bind-mounts host /usr/lib into container which shadowed packaged files.

Patch attempts tried locally (results):
- Rebase container to match host driver major: created image with CUDA 12.1 runtime to match PyTorch build -> reduced frequency but not full elimination.
- Explicitly unset LD_PRELOAD in entrypoint -> uncovered that LD_PRELOAD was indeed hiding symbol resolution problems in ~30% of reproductions; helped some cases.
- Force ldconfig after container start to prefer /usr/local/cuda/lib64 -> reduced 'undefined symbol' imports but still saw OOMs.
- Updated nvidia-container-toolkit to 1.14.1 on one node -> no repro for 48h but other nodes still failing.
- Downgraded host driver to 535.54 (trial) -> temporarily stopped the 'unknown error (303)' but produced different kernel messages (Xid 79).

Hypotheses and reasoning:
- Hypothesis A: Mixed libcuda artifacts between host and image + ldconfig/LD_LIBRARY_PATH order mismatch cause occasional symbol lookups to resolve to a wrong variant (older minor/patch) leading to undefined symbols or inconsistent ABI at runtime.
  - Evidence: ldd shows host libcuda is bind-mounted and an older compat shim present in /etc/ld.so.preload on failing hosts. Unsetting LD_PRELOAD reduces failures.
- Hypothesis B: Driver ABI flakiness at particular driver/kernel combo + MPS/plugin interactions cause an intermittent failure on first allocation (returns UNKNOWN instead of OOM) and leaves GPU in a state that next process sees as out-of-memory.
  - Evidence: dmesg Xid entries and kernel log correlation with first allocation calls.
- Hypothesis C: bitsandbytes or other native extension loads custom mmap/allocator that races with cuda runtime initialization causing fragmentation at startup and immediate OOMs for medium-sized allocations.
  - Evidence: failures correlate with images that preinstall bitsandbytes and enable custom CUDA kernels.

Next steps to validate (short experiments):
1) Minimal container that mounts no host directories except /dev/nvidia* + /proc + /sys and sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to /usr/local/cuda/lib64 only; run repro and log full loader resolution (LD_DEBUG=libs). Expectation: if failures reduce, host bind-mounting is culprit.
   - command snippet:
     docker run --rm --gpus all --name test --env LD_DEBUG=libs --cap-add SYS_PTRACE
       --volume /dev:/dev:ro
       --volume /proc:/proc:ro
       --volume /sys:/sys:ro
       --env LD_PRELOAD=
       my-cuda-minimal:12.1 python -c "import torch; torch.cuda.init();" 2>&1 | tee ld-debug.log
2) Reproduce with strace and LD_DEBUG=solver to get symbol resolution timeline for libcuda and libcudart.
3) Run small microbench that allocates many small tensors vs one big contiguous allocation to see fragmentation pattern.
4) Build a container image that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to container-provided CUDA libs and creates a wrapper that fails fast if host libcuda is available in container (fail early with explicit check).

Temporary mitigations we can apply cluster-wide (safe trials):
- Ensure nvidia-container-toolkit mounts do not inadvertently bind host /usr/lib into container images (audit runtime config).
- Add entrypoint that unsets LD_PRELOAD and forces LD_LIBRARY_PATH to container-cuda lib64 before any Python import. Roll as canary to a small fleet.
- Add startup smoke test in node agent that runs a tiny cudaInit() in a sandboxed container and reports symbol mismatch or initial allocation errors before scheduling user containers.

Notes / gotchas observed: 
- Some images that 'worked' on one host fail on another even though driver versions match — suspect packaging differences: vendor-specific libs (libnvidia-ml.so.*) and dpkg postinst create symlinks differently.
- OCI hooks from monitoring stack added a ld.so preload entry on a subset of hosts; those preloads were never intended for inference containers but the hook file is global.
- Reproducing locally is brittle: sometimes a reboot clears GPU state and the bug disappears for a day. This suggests the failure path leaves GPU state in a bad condition (supports Hypothesis B).

Log snippets to keep (for ticket):
- Import failure: "ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: undefined symbol: cuMemAlloc_v2"
- Kernel Xid from dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=4221, GPU has fallen off the bus"
- LD_DEBUG resolution order showing libcuda resolved from /usr/local/lib/libcuda.so (old shim) instead of /usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so

Questions for team:
- Who owns the node startup hooks that write /etc/ld.so.preload (SRE? infra-image)? We should audit and conditionally disable for inference nodes.
- Can we add a container-level ldconfig at entrypoint that prefers container-cuda? Risk: performance implication unknown.
- Is there a safe, rapid smoke check we can run in autoscaler to detect nodes in bad state (e.g., tiny allocation + cuMemGetInfo)?

Decision/next actions (short list):
- [ ] Run minimal no-host-bind container experiment on 3 failing nodes (Aisha)
- [ ] Add canary entrypoint that unsets LD_PRELOAD and forces container LD_LIBRARY_PATH to small fleet (Tom)
- [ ] Open JIRA OPS-987 with error logs + dmesg Xid timestamps and assign to infra (Diego)
- [ ] Draft cluster node smoke-test PR to agent (small python cudaInit + allocation) and roll to staging (Aisha/Tom)

If I have time: capture full LD_DEBUG=libs output, annotate symbol resolution timeline, and attach to the JIRA. Also try run with bitsandbytes disabled to isolate allocator effect.

End of scratchpad.
